title: Gesture-Based Physical Collaboration with Humanoid Robots
description: We are developing humanoid robots that can coordinate with people through natural body language, not just explicit commands. This project focuses on robots that can read human gestures such as pointing, glancing, beckoning, or offering an object; infer what a person wants in a shared physical scene; and respond through safe, legible whole-body motion. Students will work on problems at the intersection of human-robot interaction, loco-manipulation, perception, control, simulation, and vision-language-action models, with applications including fetching pointed-to objects, handing items to people, receiving objects from them, putting things away, and asking clarifying questions when a request is ambiguous. The goal is to build robots that are not only capable manipulators, but also intuitive collaborators that can participate in everyday, wordless physical exchanges with humans.
